narrative: Your predicted probability of leaving is 80%, meaning the model sees a very high risk that you will exit soon; on that basis, promotion was denied. The strongest signal is your total work experience of 6–10 years. Compared with employees predicted to stay—where half have only 1–5 years—your broader experience makes a move to another employer more plausible. The second signal is your 1–5 years with this organization. Although this tenure is common among stayers, combined with your overall experience it suggests you are in a mobile career stage rather than deeply settled here. Third, and most distinctive, you reported having other job opportunities. Only about one in four employees predicted to stay said the same, so this strongly pushes the prediction toward leaving. Your low salary band, lack of bonus, feeling you did not get the deserved promotion, low emotional commitment, and weak sense of job stability add to that risk. Given this, the organization should not simply treat denial as a filter; it should review whether pay, recognition, career path, and promotion timing are competitive. You should clarify what would make staying worthwhile and whether the denied promotion can be reassessed with a clear development plan.
